target_customer: Engineers, product companies and online sellers needing batches of 3D printed parts or print on demand fulfillment
problem: Desktop 3D printing could not deliver parts at volume and speed; Voodoo ran a robot assisted farm of hundreds of printers to make thousands of parts on demand.
business_model: 3D printing service bureau, per part and per order, plus Fulfilled by Voodoo print on demand for online sellers
product_category: On demand manufacturing / 3D printing service bureau

founders.name: Max Friefeld
education: Harvey Mudd College, computer and electrical engineering (2013)

founders.name: Jon Miller Schwartz
founders.background_notes: Later Body Labs and Arena AI per YC page

founders.name: Oliver Ortlieb
education: Harvey Mudd College, BS computer science
founders.background_notes: Holds several 3D printing patents per YC page

founders.name: Patrick Deem
founders.role: CFO and head of business development

exit.reason: Company statement cited COVID-19 financial strain after its factory pivoted to protective equipment such as face shields; trade press added high operating costs. Its critical assets were later bought by 3D Printing Tech of Atlanta (announced the following March, about 2021-03).

competitors.name: MakeXYZ
competitors.what: Distributed model sending print jobs to local owners of 3D printers

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliably running 200 plus identical consumer printers needed custom racks, robot handling and job software; the underlying printers were off the shelf MakerBot Replicator 2 units.

defensibility.rationale: Capital and operating know how in a farm of cheap printers; any competitor could buy the same printers, and customers had low switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it; the company shut in 2020 and its assets were bought by a small Atlanta printing firm.

market_need_then: Press in 2015 described service bureaus as focused on low volume high value parts, leaving a gap for fast volume runs of plastic parts; the founders had run a 3D printing portal since 2012 and saw the demand there.

branding.domain_note: voodoomfg.com used as the company domain (shortened mfg form); acquisition history not found
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Fortune, TechCrunch and trade press at launch in 2015, mainly for the robot printer farm rather than the name.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable name and decent trade press, but no evidence the name drove growth or that fans or merch existed.

pivots.to: Face shield production for COVID-19 response
pivots.why: Pandemic demand and to keep the factory running; over 15,000 shields reported

outcome_analysis: Voodoo built a distinctive robot assisted printer farm and raised a small seed round from KPCB Edge, but the business was a capital heavy service bureau with low switching costs in a crowded 3D printing market. When COVID-19 hit in 2020 the face shield pivot could not cover high Brooklyn operating costs, and the company closed in August 2020, with assets sold later to 3D Printing Tech.
notes: One search snippet says total funding was $6.7M; only the $1.4M KPCB Edge seed is from a fetched article, the rest is unverified. Seed date not stated. Competition list is thin because only one dated competitor was found. YC page was fetched; the company website was not fetched and is presumed dead.
